newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has denied that the government ordered the suspension of a TV programme featuring major pre-election political debates, but said that the Cabinet had discussed the "bias" of the moderators and would "keep a closer" look on the programme. The controversy stemmed from the debate aired on Channel 9 on Monday night between rivals Chuan Leekpai and Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who both aspire to be prime minister. (THE NATION)

- Police are stepping up efforts to stop counterfeiting of U.S. banknotes in Thailand, enlisting cooperation of the U.S. Secret Service. U.S. officials have told police that the quality of the counterfeits is high, especially those produced by the Red Japanese syndicate which look very much like genuine "greenbacks". (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister and Interior Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has decided to withhold an order to temporarily open border checkpoints in four provinces bordering Cambodia. The decision to withhold the order was made after accusations of Banharn's support for the Khmer Rouge. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa is expected to give a green light today for building a deep sea port in the southern Phang-nga province. Some former Democrat members of parliament have accused the government of trying to shelve the Southern Seaboard Development Project when it decided to scale down a proposed motorway. (MANAGER)

- The Bank of Thailand plans to streamline its foreign reserve management by setting up three different portfolios -- domestic liquidity management, matching public sector foreign exchange liabilities, and investment. The central bank will have to create a benchmark for each of the portfolios to measure its performance. (THE NATION)
